Hey guys with all this controversy about Siege of Dragonspear I have become interested in the Baldur's Gate series, which I think I would enjoy as a player of Dungeons and Dragons.

I was wondering what advantages the Enhanced Edition has over the original edition of the game, or if I am better off just getting the original.

I would love to hear your input. Comment away!
WSIG: Baldur's Gate Original or Enhanced Edition

The Enhanced Edition was incompatible with mods that already existed for the original game, though some mods have been updated to work around that.

The Enhanced Edition had some bug fixes, resolution changes and such. Most of those were available through mods already.

Basically, the Enhanced Edition rewrote some engine parts to work better on newer systems, while the original could have those changes done via mods.

Better off with the original.
Beamdog's original plan was to do an HD remake of BG1. Then they realized the original art assets were nowhere to be found. Oops. Plan B: Enhanced Edition!

Personally, I'm a purist, and it's the originals or bust.

That being said, it appears the EE have loads and loads of bugfixes. Things I never even realized were a problem when I played the game as a teenager. Like monsters not having the correct resistances, NPCs not wandering around, etc. It's probably safe to say they don't correct any crucial bugs, but "crucial" might be in the eye of the beholder.

There are however a smattering of new NPCs you can recruit, and I've always heard the writing for them was incredibly jarring. The tone doesn't even remotely match the original game. In retrospect, this should have been the canary in the coal mine. Even when the EE first came out, people were thrilled at modern resolution options and bug fixes, but lukewarm to negative about the added content, scant as it was. Most people concluded that you could always just avoid it.

Definitely get the originals, not EE. I'm personally going to re-download my installers and preserve them to make sure they never get tainted by Beamdog's SJWery. Might even make them available for those who sail the seven seas if you catch my meaning - that's how pissed I am at Beamdog.
Whatever you gotta to do to preserve art!
I've got EE last weekend, it works fine, I can't compare it though. With a 4K or wide screen, proper scaling is important, before changing the settings it only used a tiny part of my screen.

Original, word has always been that the "enhanced editions" are buggier. Plus there's a free mod (tutu, but it requires the original Baldur's Gate 2 to work) that gives you the graphical enhancements from the enhanced edition as well.

Baldur's Gate II is one of the best RPGs of all time. Probably the longest game in existence as well.

One advantage others haven't mentioned is that the Enhanced Edition will run on some new platforms like iPad (I find it works quite well here)

So unfortunate that Beamdog seems determined to ruin any new content; but at least they didn't fuck with the original writing afaik; the enhanced editions are basically just modern ports with bug fixes.

The enhanced editions are great, except everything that Beamdog added. So the inclusion of bug fixes are great, automatic scaling to modern resolutions is great, steam achievements are great. However, everything they themselves added instead of simply brought up to modern standards is not good. The new characters are rigid and out of place, and perhaps more importantly the new UI is an abomination and there is no way to disable it or toggle back to the old one.

If not for the UI, I'd probably reluctantly suggest the enhanced editions simply because I think having permanent access to the game rather than having to keep an installer around is nice. And I think achievements are fun. However, since you can't disable Beamdog's UI changes, I'd suggest going with the original and simply make sure to grab all the mods that bring it up to date with modern systems similar to the changes Beamdog natively integrated.
